Seraphel inclines her head.

“The tune is very short; the pleasure is the chase.  
Each singer enters late, then finds another’s place.”

“It sounds deliberately inconvenient,” Thessaly says.

“It is,” Seraphel replies. “That’s why it survives a crowded place.”

Aldric, farther down the table, looks up from his plate. “Is it difficult?”

“Not difficult,” Seraphel says. “Just easy to spoil.”

That earns a small laugh from Rashid. Ashara reaches for another carrot, apparently content to let the subject remain harmless.

You listen, then give your attention back to the meal: peppered vegetables, warm bread, the low traffic of ordinary conversation around the candlelit table.
